contentFull:
Review: Why nutrition is gaining importance for pig health

Pig health is no longer the exclusive domain of veterinary stakeholders. As preventing disease is of growing importance, the role of nutrition grows accordingly. So how can nutrition help? That was the message of a one-day scientific event, held just before this year’s International Pig Veterinary Society (IPVS) Congress, in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, on June 16.

Vincent ter BeekEditor of Pig Progress / Topic: Pigs around the world

Jul 31

Prof Nadia Everaert during her presentation in Ho Chi Minh City. Photo: Adisseo

Animal nutrition company Adisseo organised the satellite event with an evocative theme: ‘Designing resilient swine systems: Gut health and nutrition-driven strategies.’ Over 50 swine nutrition and health experts from all over the world heard resilience being defined as “the ability of a pig to recover quickly after a disturbance or stress and return to its original state or function.”

Resilient pigs and an optimal microbiota

Prof Nadia Everaert of KU Leuven, Belgium gave that definition. She was one of the speakers at the satellite event. Her presentation contained the heart of the event’s message: the road to resilient animals also leads through the pigs’ guts. One component of achieving resilience is to make sure the complex of gut bacteria (i.e. the microbiota) is in an optimal condition, she said.

Obviously, the main question therefore was: which factors influence the development of the gut microbiota? To that end, she discussed:

the host’s genetics;

maternal transmission and milk composition;

the environment (including hygiene and litter materials);

weaning interventions (for instance weaning age and creep feeding)

additives targeting the microbiota, like prebiotics, probiotics or symbiotics; and

welfare, for instance reduced stress levels.

Pig nutrition and resilience

Prof Dominiek Maes, attached to Ghent University, Belgium, kicked off the event. After giving an overview of pig production figures all over the planet, he delved into the question of which health issues occurred where across the globe. He said that nutrition plays an important role in making animals more resilient, seeing that this is usually 70% of the costs of production. Animal resilience, he said, is likely to get more emphasis as fewer antibiotics are going to be used. He concluded, “The question is not only how efficiently pigs grow under optimal conditions, but how well they cope when things go wrong”,

Biosecurity, vaccination and detection

Not only nutrition ought to receive attention, as obviously the first line of defence for optimal resilience is composed of biosecurity, vaccination and early detection. Associate professor Romeo Sanchez of the University of the Philippines, Los Baños explored that further. He discussed each of the aspects in clear and thorough detail and gave practical, sometimes Asian, examples. He stated that African Swine Fever (ASF) is currently the most important challenge in the region. The best way to deal with it is to eradicate the disease, as there are currently no good treatments available and living with the disease is not affordable in the long term.

ALSO READ: Pig health involves more than just attention for single pathogens

Achieving resilience through precision feeding

Prof Defa Li provided the last presentation of the event. He is attached to the Feed Research Chain of the Chinese Ministry of Agricultural and Rural Affairs Feed Industry Centre (Mafic). The topic of his talk was “Turning science into practice.” According to him, Mafic uses numerous novel precision feeding models to achieve optimal feed efficiency and thus optimal animal resilience. He mentioned dynamic prediction models through a feed database; precision nutrient delivery systems, pre-digestion technologies as well as the use of digestion and fermentation kinetics models. Together, these tools and approaches enable more precise and effective nutritional strategies, strengthening animal health, robustness and resilience.
translationZh:
猪健康不再是兽医相关方的专属领域。随着疾病预防的重要性日益提升，营养的作用也随之增长。那么营养能如何发挥作用？这是今年6月16日在越南胡志明市举办的国际猪兽医学会（IPVS）大会前一天举行的一场科学研讨会的主题。

动物营养公司Adisseo组织了这场卫星活动，主题颇具启发性：“设计韧性猪系统：肠道健康与营养驱动策略”。来自全球的50多位猪营养与健康专家齐聚一堂，将韧性定义为“猪在受到干扰或应激后迅速恢复并回到原有状态或功能的能力”。

**韧性猪与最佳微生物群**

比利时鲁汶大学的Nadia Everaert教授给出了这一定义。她是该卫星活动的演讲者之一。她的演讲包含了活动核心信息：通往韧性动物的道路也经过猪的肠道。她说，实现韧性的一个组成部分是确保肠道细菌复合体（即微生物群）处于最佳状态。

因此，主要问题显然是：哪些因素影响肠道微生物群的发育？为此，她讨论了：

- 宿主的遗传；
- 母体传播和乳汁成分；
- 环境（包括卫生和垫料材料）；
- 断奶干预措施（例如断奶日龄和补饲）；
- 针对微生物群的添加剂，如益生元、益生菌或合生元；以及
- 福利，例如降低应激水平。

**猪营养与韧性**

比利时根特大学的Dominiek Maes教授为活动开场。在概述了全球猪生产数据后，他深入探讨了全球各地出现的健康问题。他说，营养在使动物更具韧性方面发挥着重要作用，因为这通常占生产成本的70%。他说，随着抗生素使用减少，动物韧性可能会受到更多重视。他总结道：“问题不仅在于猪在最佳条件下生长效率如何，还在于当出现问题时它们如何应对。”

**生物安全、疫苗接种和检测**

不仅营养应受到关注，因为最佳韧性的第一道防线显然由生物安全、疫苗接种和早期检测组成。菲律宾大学洛斯巴尼奥斯分校的Romeo Sanchez副教授对此进行了深入探讨。他清晰而详尽地讨论了各个方面，并给出了实用的、有时是亚洲的例子。他说，非洲猪瘟（ASF）目前是该地区最重要的挑战。应对它的最佳方法是根除该病，因为目前没有好的治疗方法，长期与疾病共存是负担不起的。

**通过精准饲喂实现韧性**

中国农业农村部饲料工业中心（Mafic）的李德发教授提供了活动的最后一场演讲。他演讲的主题是“将科学转化为实践”。据他介绍，Mafic使用多种新型精准饲喂模型来实现最佳饲料效率，从而实现最佳动物韧性。他提到了通过饲料数据库进行动态预测模型；精准营养输送系统；预消化技术以及消化和发酵动力学模型的使用。总之，这些工具和方法能够实现更精准有效的营养策略，增强动物健康、健壮性和韧性。
author: Vincent ter Beek
